text:
incidents-bot: [ALERT] Elevated 5xx rate detected for /v1/generate on inference-gateway (private-vpc egress). 5xx spike ~18% over 5m. Affected tenant: corp-enterprise-42. Pager notified.

maria-sre: ack. I'm oncall. paging network and eng. @sara-net @omar-eng can you take a look? Seeing lots of 502/504 in gateway logs.

omar-eng: looking at gateway logs now — upstream connections to customer egress IPs are resetting. Lots of TLS handshake errors to 10.2.13.5:443 and 10.2.13.6:443. 502 responses from our proxy layer.

sara-net: checking VPC flow logs and nat metrics. Flow logs show lots of SYN from nodes -> internet, replies sometimes returning to different private IPs. That screams asymmetric SNAT mapping; possible NAT port depletion or sticky mapping chaos.

maria-sre: customer CS ping: "we're getting 504 timeouts across endpoints since ~20:05 UTC". tagging @customer-success-amy for live updates.

customer-success-amy: confirming, they've reported widespread timeouts for inference calls and some retries causing duplicate charges on their end. They want ETA.

omar-eng: running quick checks on nodes:
```
# on gateway node
ss -s
# shows high TIME_WAIT and large number of ephemeral ports in use
conntrack -S
# shows conntrack entries near limit for 10.2.0.0/16
```

omar-eng: also pulled a sample stacktrace from the proxy: upstream connect failed: connection refused / reset. Not application errors, network resets.

sara-net: digging into infra change history — I see a customer-side change rolled out at 19:50: "egress-sg-tightening" that added stricter egress port ranges and pinned outbound source port ranges (weird). Also see a recent NAT gateway health event at 20:00 where one NAT IP flapped. Might be combined effect.

maria-sre: hypothesis: NAT port depletion + asymmetric routing from route table change causing responses to land on different NAT IPs -> upstream TLS state mismatch -> 502/504. Could also be conntrack exhaustion for the customer CIDR.

omar-eng: quick_probe: curl -v https://example-external/ from a node shows handshake then immediate reset intermittently.

sara-net: I can try a mitigation: fail traffic for the tenant's CIDR to nat-gw-2 (alternate NAT with larger ephemeral pool) by adjusting the egress route table for 10.2.12.0/22. That should restore consistent SNAT IP and reduce asymmetric flows.

kevin-pd: agree with mitigation. Maria, if you want to hand off to night oncall after swap, please share steps. I'll coordinate with infra to make sure the route change is approved.

maria-sre: proceeding with controlled failover. Steps: 1) update route table RT-outer -> target nat-gw-2 for CIDR 10.2.12.0/22, 2) monitor 5xx rate and flow logs, 3) if improved, leave for night team to follow-up on root cause.

deploy-bot: queued change: route-table-update RT-outer -> nat-gw-2 for 10.2.12.0/22 (manual apply). Change owner: sara-net. ETA apply 2m.

sara-net: applied route swap. Monitoring.

omar-eng: immediate metrics: 5xx rate dropped from 18% -> 6% in first two minutes. latency still a little high but trending down. Some retries still failing (likely clients with cached connections to old SNAT IP).

maria-sre: good. next mitigations: 1) request customer to rotate their client connections (short-lived TLS) or we can purge platform-level connection cache for that tenant prefix to force new handshakes, 2) ask infra to request provider increase ephemeral port pool on nat-gw-2 and check autoscale settings.

sara-net: started port pool increase request with cloud team. Also found a rule in customer's egress ACL that restricts source port range -> asked them to relax to ephemeral range 32768-61000. They've acknowledged.

omar-eng: purged prefix cache for tenant on proxy: 
```
# proxy admin
POST /admin/prefix-cache/purge
{ "prefix": "10.2.12.0/22" }
```
That should drop existing NAT-mapped sessions and force reconnects.

customer-success-amy: passing to customer: they're rotating clients now, seeing immediate improvement from some hosts. Thanks.

maria-sre: monitoring 5xx: now at 1.8% over 5m, down to baseline. Impact reduced; still watching for residual errors.

incidents-bot: Incident status changed: SEV2 (reduced from SEV1). Paging suppressed.

kevin-pd: planning handoff. Maria — any follow-ups for night oncall?

maria-sre: handoff summary for night team (@omar-eng):
- Incident: Elevated 5xx / 504 from private-vpc tenant corp-enterprise-42 due to NAT SNAT port exhaustion and asymmetric egress after tenant ACL change and a NAT IP flap.
- Current state: traffic routed through nat-gw-2; 5xx back to baseline. Customer rotating clients and relaxing source port rule. Port pool increase requested with cloud team (in progress).
- Actions for night: verify cloud port pool increase applied, check NAT autoscale logs, confirm no conntrack saturations recur, follow up with customer to verify no data loss / retry billing concerns.
- Runbook refs: runbook/networking/nat-port-depletion, runbook/incidents/vpc-egress-handbook.

omar-eng: taking handoff. I have the temporary route change in place. I'll keep monitoring and will open a follow-up ticket to root-cause with infra and customer.

maria-sre: thanks team. closing active mitigation window, leaving postmortem task for tomorrow.

incidents-bot: Incident thread closed for active mitigation. Please file postmortem if recurring.
